claims.text: A high-entropy spinel oxide containing Cr, Mn, Fe, Co, and Ni can be formed from a homogeneously mixed precursor.
The proposed spinel oxide contains a minor or trace amount of Pt.
Solventless thermolysis can synthesize medium- and high-entropy spinel oxides from molecular precursors.
A controlled solid-state or solventless thermolysis route will ensure high configurational disorder in the proposed five-metal spinel.
Trace Pt can be doped into this high-entropy spinel with atomic-level dispersion.
Increasing configurational disorder in multimetal spinel oxides improves CO oxidation performance.
Enhanced configurational disorder produces a higher density of oxygen vacancies.
Enhanced configurational disorder strengthens Pt–spinel metal-support interactions.
The stronger metal-support interactions stabilize trace Pt and preserve active sites.
Lattice disorder facilitates oxygen-vacancy formation and improves oxygen mobility.
Improved oxygen mobility promotes regeneration of active Pt sites.
The proposed vacancy-mediated pathway lowers the CO oxidation light-off temperature.
Improved Pt–support interactions minimize Pt sintering and deactivation during cyclic redox operation.
More highly disordered spinel oxides resist catalyst deactivation better than less disordered spinel oxides.
The Pt-doped high-entropy spinel will have a markedly lower T10 for CO oxidation than conventional higher-Pt-loaded Pt/ceria catalysts.
The Pt-doped high-entropy spinel will retain higher catalytic activity during prolonged cycling than conventional Pt/ceria catalysts.
The proposed catalyst will match or exceed conventional Pt/ceria performance while using significantly less Pt.
The predicted activity and durability improvements will hold from 200 to 500 °C under automotive cyclic redox conditions.

contradictions.description: The initial precursor is described as already incorporating minor Pt, whereas the intervention says Pt is doped only after formation of the high-entropy spinel, leaving the synthesis sequence inconsistent.
